title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-maya-singh
body:
Account: Acme Health (acme-health)
Priority: High — heavy inference use (NLP triage), regulated PHI data, US east coast ops
Intro: Met with Sam (head of AI infra) at HLTH conf — good fit for Dedicated / Private options. Interested in predictable latency and SOC2-level compliance.

Key stakeholders (from LinkedIn / notes):
- Samir Caldwell — Head of AI Infrastructure (decision influencer)
- Priya Rao — Director of Clinical Data Platforms (data residency/security lead)
- Ben Torres — CTO (final sign-off for infra spend)
- SalesOps: Jaime (procurement)

Quick account signals / tech profile:
- Currently using a mix of managed cloud GPUs + a small internal serving layer (closed-source).
- Volume: ~40M inference tokens / month (estimate) across triage + summarization pipelines.
- Latency sensitivity: 99th pctl < 300ms for triage user flows.
- Compliance: HIPAA + contractual BAAs required.
- Region: US-East primary; exploring private VPC for PHI flows.

Pain points they mentioned / inferred:
- Cost overruns during batch jobs — spikes cause unpredictable billing and throttling.
- Poor observability across model versions; app teams nervous about silent regressions.
- Need for deterministic throughput for clinician-facing apps (SLOs).

Value props relevant to them:
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity to smooth throughput and predict costs.
- Private deployment + KMS integrations for PHI/BAA compliance.
- Console + Rollouts: can do canary + automatic fallback to reduce regression risk.
- Optimize recommendations: batching/caching profiles to cut cost on high-volume pipelines.

Outbound drafts (short + long):
1) Short cold email (subject lines):
- Subject: cut inference costs 30% while keeping clinician SLOs
- Subject: predictable latency for Acme Health triage workflows

Email body (short):
Hi Samir —
We met briefly at HLTH — I was following up with a quick note: Redwood helps health platforms like Acme lock in predictable inference throughput and compliance (VPC + KMS + BAA). For triage workflows you described, teams typically see 20–40% cost reduction from prefix caching + batching and remove the worst latency spikes with reserved capacity.
Can we do a 20-min call next week to see if a small Dedicated pilot (1 month) makes sense?
Thanks,
Maya

2) Longer outreach / sequence step 2 (after no reply):
Hi Priya / Samir —
Following up on my note about a pilot. Quick details so you can share internally:
- Pilot scope: 2-week performance baseline -> 4-week Dedicated pilot with same model family, no code changes.
- Success metrics: 95th pctl latency reduction, cost per 1k tokens, and zero-regression on a set of 10 golden prompts.
- Compliance: Private control plane + KMS integration; we can sign BAA.
If you can point me to the person who owns vendor security sign-off, I can loop them in and share our SOC2/BAA checklist. Thoughts?

Call script (15-min intro):
- 0:00–2:00 quick intros + context from HLTH
- 2:00–6:00 understand workloads: model family, avg seq length, QPS, SLOs
- 6:00–9:00 current infra pain / procurement process / timeline
- 9:00–13:00 propose pilot + success metrics (see above)
- 13:00–15:00 next steps (security checklist, PO, trial access)

Objection handling (common):
- "We're happy with cloud provider endpoints" -> A: Great — many teams start there; Redwood can sit in front as a routing layer to reduce cost with batching + caching and give you predictable SLAs without rip-and-replace.
- "We can't move PHI to a third party" -> A: We offer Private deployment + on-prem option; control plane can be customer-hosted and we integrate with your KMS/HSM.
- "Procurement takes forever / legal asks for lots of docs" -> A: Offer: quick trust package (SOC2, BAA template, security questionnaire), propose PoC that isolates non-PHI traffic first.
- "We don't want vendor lock-in" -> A: We support same model APIs, can pin model versions, and have rollback/fallback to open model variants. We focus on making exit easy.

Competitive notes / positioning vs. others:
- Compared to big cloud endpoints: better batching/caching defaults + unified routing across hosted/dedicated/private -> lower unit cost + less engineering lift.
- Compared to self-hosted runtimes: we provide managed ops + rollouts and dedicated pools so you get both control and less ops overhead.

Open questions / data to collect pre-call:
- Exact model families they use (Llama vX? mix of closed models?)
- Typical sequence lengths (avg, 95p) and tokenization info
- Current 95th/99th pctl latencies and what infra they serve from (instance types)
- Any existing caching / prefix reuse in their stack

Quick TODOs (my notes):
- [ ] Find Samir's direct email (he said use firstname.lastname@acmehealth.com) — check HLTH attendee list + LinkedIn
- [ ] Pull SOC2 + BAA template into Drive share (ask legal for the latest)
- [ ] Draft one-pager tailored to Acme with expected cost delta (use Optimize playbook)
- [ ] Loop in Olivia (solutions eng) to scope pilot technical checklist
- [ ] Create a short eval prompt set (10 prompts) for golden traffic — ask Priya for anonymized examples

Slack refs / follow-up links:
- slack:#enterprise-sales thread: "Acme pilot interest" (pings to Olivia on 2024-11-06)
- Confluence: ACME-PILOT-ONE-PAGER (linked above)
- GitHub: repo for eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness (internal fork)

Notes to self (scratchy):
- prioritize PHI/BAA early -> procurement gate is security sign-off; get security checklist before PoC
- cost numbers are fuzzy — need Solutions to run cost sim quickly with their rough QPS numbers
- mention dedicated autoscale + burst capacity as a middle ground for uncertain volume

End of doc.
